originality.rationale: Six published-finding corpus semantic queries and primary-source searches did not yield an identical or stronger all-size classification. The nearest physically relevant full text, Vieira and Gonçalves (1998), has a 1D-chain/random short-bond Hamiltonian and all-spin Curie–Weiss interaction rather than two populations connected off matching; its phase formulas do not imply the exact matched-bipartite threshold/count. Other noted work treats Coulombically frustrated lattices. Generic independent-spin minimization is acknowledged prior technique; publication priority remains provisional.
residual_risks: An equivalent result may be published under signed complete bipartite, two-sublattice Curie–Weiss dimer, or mean-field paired-spin terminology not indexed by published-finding corpus/search.
The 2023 two-subensemble article and 2000 Coulomb-frustration paper were not compared via complete full text; no whole-document noncoverage is claimed.
Generic variational principles may subsume this as a special case if a sufficiently explicit general theorem is found.

value.rationale: The deterministic matched-coupling perturbation of an antiferromagnetic dense bipartite system yields a full zero-temperature phase classification on all sizes, a parity correction in the first-order threshold and a discontinuous extensive ground-state entropy. The exact finite-size degeneracy and sharp entropy boundary provide a natural tractable frustrated-network benchmark beyond a local exercise.
